reason: A water tank is needed to store the recovered heat, but the available parts do not make its assembly sequence clear.
expectation: The compatibility list should show whether the steel can be made into a tank or another useful component.

effect: The steel and service tool made a vented tank for non-potable heating water; it still needs the heat-transfer coil and water.
reaction: The separate coolant coil makes the heat-storage setup clearer.
reason: Coolant tubing should form the separate coil inside the tank.
expectation: The tubing will be fitted as a heat-transfer coil in the tank.

effect: The tank now has a sealed coil to transfer heat into separate heating water.
reaction: The separation of the two fluids makes physical sense.
reason: The tank needs water to store the recovered heat.
expectation: The tank will be filled with water around the heating coil.

effect: The drinking water supply could not be combined with the tank directly, so filling it may require another preparation or connection first.
reaction: That was unexpected; the reason is not yet clear.
reason: The tank needs insulation to retain stored warmth, so I will try fitting it before connecting the system.
expectation: The insulation will wrap the tank and reduce heat loss.

alternatives.reason: The tank might need to be connected before it can be filled.

effect: The tank is insulated and ready to fill, with its vent and fittings accessible.
reaction: The fold-back insulation gives the stored heat a practical way to reach the room.
reason: The prepared tank is now ready for water.
expectation: The tank will fill with water around the separate heating coil.

effect: The insulated tank is filled around the separate coil and remains vented; it is ready for a heat source.
reaction: The separate fluid paths make the arrangement clear.
reason: The indoor heat-recovery connection should supply process heat to the tank's coil.
expectation: The coil will connect to the process loop and warm the stored water.

effect: Connecting the coil to the process loop warmed the stored water and completed the goal; a thermostat limits its temperature.
reaction: The finished heat-recovery system gives the earlier preparations a clear purpose.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the tank to the process loop was the most worthwhile moment: it brought the separate coil, water and insulation together into a physically understandable heat store.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to fill the tank was the least worthwhile passage. The feedback did not explain why filling had to wait until after insulation.

surprise.text: I expected the tank with its coil to accept water immediately, so the rejection surprised me; insulating it first made filling possible.

arbitrary.text: Requiring insulation before filling felt somewhat arbitrary: the result established that sequence, but did not explain why filling first would be impossible.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter: the practical construction and explanations of fluid separation and heat recovery were engaging, despite the unexplained ordering constraint.
